libraries.conflict: {conflict} Use “Edit library” to change the folders.

remove.description: Cinemion forgets this library and its watch history. The files in its folders are not touched.

videos.name: Videos
videos.description: For home videos, recordings and anything else that isn't a movie or show. Nothing is looked up online: titles come from the file names, and you can edit the details by hand.

music.name: Music
music.description: Albums, artists and tracks, sorted by the tags in the files (or folders like Artist/Album/01 Title.mp3). Covers come from the files or a cover.jpg next to them, and lyrics from tags or .lrc files. Nothing is looked up online.

photos.name: Photos
photos.description: Photos and phone videos, with every folder as an album. Dates, cameras and places come from the photos themselves (HEIC from iPhones works too), and nothing is looked up online. Everyone can also make their own albums without moving any files.

clips.name: Clips
clips.description: Game recordings, grouped by game. The game comes from the names recorders give their files and folders (NVIDIA, AMD, Xbox Game Bar, OBS, Steam and more), with covers from Steam. Clips without a game can be given one by hand, or get a suggestion from picture recognition.

audiobooks.name: Audiobooks
audiobooks.description: A folder of audio files is one book (parts in CD1, CD2… folders too), and so is a single .m4b. Chapters come from the files, details from their tags, and everyone keeps their own place.

books.name: Books
books.description: EPUB books are read right in Cinemion, with everyone's place saved; PDFs open in the browser's own viewer. Details and covers come from the files.

videos.description: Profiles with an age limit only see videos rated within it. Pick “{rating}” for family videos everyone may see.

contents.text: Every backup has the database, the sign-in key, profile pictures and artwork you picked or uploaded by hand. Conversions, seek thumbnails and other things in the cache are left out; they're made again when needed.

https.intro: A secure address for Cinemion, without setting up a reverse proxy. Browsers need it for offline downloads and for notifications on phones.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.facts: From {issuer}, valid until {date}. It's renewed by itself before it runs out.

cinemion.text: Works on any home network, no domain needed. Cinemion signs its own certificate, so each device has to trust Cinemion once (see below); until then browsers warn about the address.

trust.title: Trust Cinemion on your devices
trust.text: Do this once on every device that opens Cinemion over https. It makes the device trust certificates this Cinemion signs, and nothing else.
trust.onPhone: On a phone or tablet, open {address} in its browser to download it there.

windows.title: Windows
windows.steps:
Open the downloaded file and choose Install Certificate.
Pick Local Machine, then Place all certificates in the following store, Browse, and Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
Finish, then restart the browser.

mac.title: Mac
mac.steps:
Open the downloaded file; Keychain Access adds it to the login keychain.
Double-click the certificate there, open Trust, and set When using this certificate to Always Trust.
Close the window and enter your password to save.

iphone.title: iPhone and iPad
iphone.steps:
Open the download address in Safari and allow the profile to download.
Go to Settings › General › VPN & Device Management, open the Cinemion profile and install it.
Then go to Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings and switch on full trust for Cinemion.

android.title: Android
android.steps:
Download the file in the browser.
Go to Settings › Security › More security settings (or Encryption & credentials) › Install a certificate › CA certificate, and pick the file.
The wording differs a little between phones; searching Settings for "certificate" finds it.

linux.title: Linux
linux.steps:
Arch: sudo trust anchor cinemion-ca.crt
Debian and Ubuntu: copy the file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run sudo update-ca-certificates.
Chrome on Linux keeps its own list: Settings › Privacy and security › Security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import.

firefox.title: Firefox (any computer)
firefox.steps: Firefox has its own list. Go to Settings › Privacy & Security › Certificates › View Certificates › Authorities › Import, pick the file and tick Trust this CA to identify websites.
